Sean Paul headlines T-Mobile Stage in Las Vegas on 21 November
sum: Sean Paul headlines the T-Mobile Stage at the T-Mobile Zone at Sphere in Las Vegas on 21 November 2026. The appearance forms part of the Formula 1 Heineken Las Vegas Grand Prix race weekend.

The Formula 1 Heineken Las Vegas Grand Prix runs from 19 to 21 November 2026, with the live music programme centred on the T-Mobile Stage at the T-Mobile Zone at Sphere. The Las Vegas Grand Prix programme places the Jamaican artist on Saturday, 21 November.

The performance takes place beneath Sphere’s Exosphere, within a festival-style race-week setting that combines live music with the wider Grand Prix experience. Natasha Bedingfield is also listed for the Saturday bill, while the event announcement names additional performances by Gorgon City, Ja Rule, Collect 200 and DJ Mandy.

The Jamaican rapper, singer and songwriter has remained a prominent dancehall voice for more than two decades. His catalogue includes the albums Dutty Rock, The Trinity, Imperial Blaze, Tomahawk Technique, Full Frequency, Live N Livin and Scorcha.

The Recording Academy credits him with a Grammy for Best Reggae Album for Dutty Rock. The album’s songs Get Busy and Temperature remain central to the profile described in the Las Vegas programme, which also points to his collaborations with Beyoncé, Sia, Clean Bandit, Dua Lipa and David Guetta. Further career details appear in the Recording Academy biography.

The Las Vegas engagement places Sean Paul’s dancehall sound alongside a broader programme of pop, electronic and hip-hop performances. The T-Mobile Zone at Sphere is part of the Grand Prix’s three-night entertainment schedule, giving the Saturday appearance a setting that is connected to both the concert programme and the race weekend.

Sean Paul’s place on the bill is specific to Saturday, 21 November 2026. The programme identifies him as the Saturday act and presents Natasha Bedingfield alongside him, while the other named performers appear elsewhere across the wider weekend schedule.

Quiñenco stock linked to CCU as S&P keeps outlook negative
sum: On October 29, 2026, S&P Global Ratings affirmed Compania Cervecerias Unidas S.A.'s BBB issuer credit rating and kept its outlook negative. The rating agency cited pressure from changing consumer habits, macroeconomic volatility and limited headroom in CCU's credit metrics.

S&P expects CCU's adjusted leverage to remain above 2.0 times in 2026 before declining below that level in 2027. The agency forecasts revenue growth of 6.3 percent in 2026 and expects the EBITDA margin to recover to 13.2 percent from 12.5 percent in 2025.

The analysis identifies Argentina as a key sensitivity for CCU's international business, while persistent inflation and weaker household purchasing power continue to weigh on discretionary consumption. S&P also views the acquisition of the remaining stake in Aguas CCU-Nestlé Chile as supportive of CCU's strategic control in the water category, although the transaction reduced accessible cash and lifted projected 2026 leverage.

CCU is a multicategory beverage company operating in Chile, Argentina, Bolivia, Colombia, Paraguay and Uruguay. S&P states that Inversiones y Rentas, a joint venture between Quiñenco and Heineken Chile, directly and indirectly owns 65.87 percent of CCU's shares, with each partner holding 50 percent of the joint venture.

This structure makes CCU's operating performance and credit trajectory relevant to Quiñenco's diversified Chilean business portfolio. The negative outlook is an assessment of CCU's credit profile rather than a direct rating action on Quiñenco.

Quiñenco's investor-relations calendar lists November 27, 2026 for its next earnings release. Investors will be watching whether the group's subsequent disclosures provide further detail on portfolio performance, capital allocation and the contribution of its operating holdings.

items.t: Heineken Holding (ENXTAM:HEIO) Stock Looks Fairly Valued Following Its 34% Run
sum: Heineken Holding shares have climbed strongly over the past year, and that move puts a fresh spotlight on whether the current price is in line with what the group is earning today. With the stock now reflecting both recent share gains and upbeat commentary from management, the key question is how much the earnings profile really supports this valuation.
- Heineken Holding has returned 33.8% over the past year, which raises a straightforward question about how much of that gain is grounded in its underlying earnings power.
- Management has pointed to solid recent sales growth and confirmed its profit outlook, which can influence how investors think about the durability and pace of future earnings.

The P/E ratio works well for Heineken Holding because earnings remain a central yardstick for how investors judge a mature consumer brand owner. On this measure, the stock trades on about 18.4x earnings, which is slightly above the beverage sector average of roughly 17.0x but well below the peer group closer to 30.4x. That mix of a small premium to the broader industry and a sizeable gap to peers points to a valuation that leans more middle of the pack than stretched when anchored to sector norms.

items.t: HEINEKEN USA AND OPENTABLE PARTNER TO REWARD AND CELEBRATE DESIGNATED DRIVERS
sum: ''There's No Such Thing As Fine to Drive" program expands, turning reservation booking into a seamless tool for responsible driving.

WHITE PLAINS, N.Y., July 27, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- HEINEKEN USA has announced a first-of-its-kind partnership with OpenTable, enabling diners to designate a driver directly in the booking process. Rooted in HEINEKEN USA's There's No Such Thing As Fine to Drive program, the partnership was sparked by a recent survey finding 71% of Americans would be more likely to make a safe ride home plan if they were prompted at time of reservation booking. The partnership will help remove the barriers to making responsible decisions and celebrate and reward the DD --"The Hero" of the night according to 58% of Americans.

"HEINEKEN has a longstanding global ambition to brew the joy of true togetherness, which means ensuring moments of connection are always enjoyed responsibly and removing barriers to moderation." said Anne de Graaf, Chief Corporate Affairs Officer at HEINEKEN USA. "By elevating the DD experience, we want to raise awareness that opting out of alcohol doesn't mean opting out of the fun. Our pioneering Heineken 0.0 ensures 100% of the social connection and zero judgment. This first-of-its-kind OpenTable partnership proves that choosing not to drink is a celebrated choice, shifting how people plan their nights out from the very first reservation."

"OpenTable is always looking for meaningful ways to connect diners and restaurants," said Reece Jones, General Manager, OpenTable Media. "We're thrilled to partner with HEINEKEN USA through OpenTable's tailored media solutions to do just that, while jointly delivering a new way to bring awareness for responsible consumption into the reservation process."
- The Inclusive Dinner Party: 49% of Americans say that drinking non-alcoholic beer helps them feel included in social moments when they are not consuming alcohol.
- The Key to a Better Experience: 82% of Americans say they can enjoy their day/night of drinking more knowing they have a safe ride home planned in advance.
- The Reservation Blindspot: 57% of Americans say that planning a designated driver/safe ride home is not something they typically think about when making restaurant or venue reservations.
